foreign_affairs_ministers.name: Stephane Dion
foreign_affairs_ministers.notable: FA Minister during the re-authorization of the Saudi LAV-III export permits (2016). His government retained the Harper-era General Dynamics Saudi contract, reversing Liberal campaign signalling.

foreign_affairs_ministers.name: Chrystia Freeland
foreign_affairs_ministers.notable: FA Minister during the Jamal Khashoggi murder (October 2018) and the subsequent partial Saudi arms 'freeze'. Prior role: Int'l Trade Minister 2015-2017 (held Saudi export signing authority).

foreign_affairs_ministers.name: Francois-Philippe Champagne
foreign_affairs_ministers.notable: Presided over the April 2020 resumption of Saudi arms permits despite the 2018 'freeze'. Also held Int'l Trade portfolio 2017-2018.

foreign_affairs_ministers.name: Melanie Joly
foreign_affairs_ministers.notable: FA Minister during the Gaza war escalation (October 2023 onward). Presided over the announced January 2024 'pause' on new Israel export permits — a pause that did NOT affect existing permits, with ~$229M in documented exports continuing.

foreign_affairs_ministers.name: Anita Anand
foreign_affairs_ministers.notable: Current FA Minister. Previously Defence Minister 2021-2023 during initial Gaza war period.

international_trade_ministers.name: Jim Carr
international_trade_ministers.notable: Int'l Trade Minister who signed the 2019 export-permit challenge defence filings. Died 2022.

international_trade_ministers.name: Mary Ng
international_trade_ministers.notable: Int'l Trade Minister during the continuation of Israel export permits through the 2023-2024 Gaza war period. Responsible for the Export and Import Permits Act signing authority at Global Affairs.

defence_ministers.name: Harjit Sajjan
defence_ministers.notable: Defence Minister during the bulk of the Liberal-era Saudi arms shipments. Six-year tenure spanning Khashoggi, the 2020 permit resumption, and 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal.

defence_ministers.name: Bill Blair
defence_ministers.notable: Defence Minister during the Gaza war period. DND procurement side of the arms pipeline during the same period Joly held the FA portfolio.

major_defence_exporters.name: General Dynamics Land Systems Canada
major_defence_exporters.notable: Holds the C$15B+ LAV-III contract to Saudi Arabia (Harper-era, Liberal-retained). Based in London, Ontario. Global Affairs Canada's largest single Canadian export permit counterparty.

major_defence_exporters.name: L3Harris WESCAM Canada
major_defence_exporters.notable: Based in Burlington, Ontario. Canadian-manufactured MX-series imaging systems documented by Project Ploughshares as exported to Israel and installed on IDF F-35 aircraft.

major_defence_exporters.name: CMC Electronics
major_defence_exporters.notable: Based in Montreal and Ottawa. Holds Canadian Controlled Goods Directorate registration. Avionics supplier to multiple NATO and non-NATO air forces.

major_defence_exporters.name: Colt Canada
major_defence_exporters.notable: Based in Kitchener, Ontario. Sole source of Canadian Armed Forces C7/C8 rifles. Export program includes documented shipments to multiple coalition and NATO allies.

export_controls_institutions.name: GAC Export Controls Division
export_controls_institutions.notable: The Global Affairs Canada unit that reviews and issues Export and Import Permits Act permits. Responsible for the human-rights risk assessment step (Arms Trade Treaty art. 7) each permit is required to receive.

export_controls_institutions.name: Controlled Goods Directorate
export_controls_institutions.notable: The Public Services and Procurement Canada directorate that registers all Canadian firms allowed to handle controlled goods (military-grade items). Maintains the registry from which Project Ploughshares builds its annual Canadian exporter census.

export_controls_institutions.name: Federal Court of Canada (arms export challenges)
export_controls_institutions.notable: The court where multiple challenges to Saudi and Israel arms export permits have been filed since 2019. Has consistently upheld GAC's permitting discretion — Turp v Canada (Foreign Affairs) 2019 FC 634 dismissed the Saudi challenge.

timeline.event: Liberal government retains Harper-era General Dynamics LAV-III export contract to Saudi Arabia (~C$15B).
timeline.source: Global Affairs Canada Export Permit Report

timeline.event: Minister Freeland authorizes issuance of export permits for ongoing LAV-III shipments to Saudi Arabia.
timeline.source: GAC Annual Report on Exports of Military Goods 2016

timeline.event: Canada signs the Arms Trade Treaty (ATT). Ratification Sept 17 2019.
Jamal Khashoggi murdered at Saudi consulate in Istanbul. Canada announces intention to 'freeze' new Saudi arms export permits.
timeline.source: Statement from the Prime Minister, Oct 22 2018

timeline.event: Federal Court dismisses Turp v Canada (Foreign Affairs) challenge to Saudi arms exports.
Canada ratifies the Arms Trade Treaty. Arts. 6 and 7 require risk-assessment of exports that could facilitate war crimes.
Minister Champagne announces resumption of Saudi arms export permits despite the 2018 'freeze'.
Hamas attack on Israel. Gaza war begins.
Canadian Israel-destined military-goods export permits remain in force.
timeline.source: GAC Annual Report on Exports of Military Goods 2023

timeline.event: Minister Joly announces 'pause' on NEW Israel export permits. Existing permits unaffected.
International Court of Justice provisional measures in South Africa v Israel find 'plausible risk of genocide'.
Canadian-made WESCAM MX imaging systems confirmed installed on IDF F-35s during Gaza campaign.
timeline.source: Project Ploughshares research + multiple press reports

timeline.event: Project Ploughshares year-to-date tally: ~C$229M in Canadian military-goods exports destined for Israel still moving under pre-Oct-2023 permits.
Continuing Federal Court challenges to Israel arms export permits. Disposition pending.

treaty_obligations: Arms Trade Treaty (ATT) — ratified by Canada 17 Sept 2019. Art. 6 prohibits exports that would facilitate serious violations of international humanitarian law. Art. 7 requires human-rights and risk assessment for every export permit.
Geneva Conventions Additional Protocol I — common article 1 requires States Party to 'ensure respect' for the Conventions in all circumstances.
Genocide Convention 1948 — Art. I obligates ratifying states to prevent genocide; arms supply despite ICJ 'plausible risk' finding raises state-responsibility question.
domestic_framework: Export and Import Permits Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. E-19)
accountability_chain.oversight_body: Global Affairs Canada Export Controls Division — issues permits; publishes annual Report on Exports of Military Goods
accountability_chain.oversight_body_limit: GAC reports after the fact; there is no independent review of individual permit approvals before issuance
judicial_remedies_filed: Turp v Canada (FA), 2019 FC 634 — Saudi arms challenge dismissed
Multiple 2024-2025 Federal Court challenges to Israel permits — pending
accountability_chain.result_2024: ~C$229M in Israel-destined Canadian military-goods exports in 2024 under pre-war permits; GDLS Saudi LAV-III contract remains active; exporters unaffected by sanctions or criminal investigations
